bottom_line: Nifty closed at 25,884 with GIFT Nifty signalling a weak start today, impacted by Middle East tensions driving Brent crude toward $97.
Jefferies upgraded MSCI India's FY27 earnings by 1%, making it a rare annual upgrade, while JP Morgan targets Nifty at 29,000 by end-2027.
Supreme Court ordered prosecution sanctions against HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank over subvention schemes, while SEBI launched a Coffee Day forensic probe.

global.us: Wall Street finished mixed in the previous session as tech stocks faced pressure, leading the Nasdaq down 0.62% while the Dow Jones rose 0.33%. Markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, leaving US stock futures to tick higher ahead of Friday's shortened Black Friday trading session.
global.europe: European equity markets posted broad gains on Thursday, led by Germany's DAX rising 2.08% and the Euro Stoxx 50 advancing 2.04%. The UK's FTSE 100 gained 1.75% supported by rallies in bank and mining equities alongside takeover interest in Imperial Brands.
global.asia: Asian markets are trading higher this morning as technology shares stabilize. South Korea's KOSPI is up 2.05% and Japan's Nikkei 225 has gained 1.01%, though gains remain capped as Tokyo core CPI accelerated to 2.9% year-on-year in November.

india: Indian equity benchmark Nifty 50 ended Thursday up 0.25% at 25,884, while the Sensex rose 0.46% to 84,329, near 10-month highs driven by IT stocks and foreign fund inflows. Bank Nifty diverged to drop 0.26%. For today's open, GIFT Nifty points to a negative start down around 37 to 80 points, weighed down by rising crude oil prices and Middle East geopolitical tensions.
commodities: Brent crude settled at $92.26 per barrel after falling 2.48%, though live morning trades pushed prices higher toward $97 amid Middle East conflict and supply threats. Gold rose 3.08% to $3,644.60 per ounce, while silver jumped 8.05% to $43.28. The Indian Rupee weakened 0.61% to close at 92.24 against the US dollar as crude pressures import bills.
